blocking_findings.summary: ASKFLOOR-1-T3a-AC4: SERVICE. NEW `application/permissions/human-decision-memory-service.ts` exporting `HumanDecisionMemoryService` (class, constructor-injected `{ repository, newId = randomUUID, now = currentIso }` — the `CapabilitySecretService` pattern, `application/capability-secrets/capability-secret-service.ts:17`; no adapter construction, port import only per `scripts/architecture-map.json`): `remember(dto: HumanDecisionRememberRequest) → { status: 'remembered'; id; shortId; scopeKey; pathOnly; stored: 'inserted' | 'refreshed' } | { status: 'not_rememberable'; reason: HumanDecisionServiceRefusal }` where `HumanDecisionServiceRefusal = HumanDecisionNotRememberableReason | 'unresolved_person' | 'once_never_remembered'` — refuses a blank `actingPersonId` (`unresolved_person`) and a `resolution` whose `kind` is not `'remember'` (`once_never_remembered`: a scalar `allow_once`/`allow_persistent_rule`/`cancel` never reaches the store) BEFORE any repository call; derives the key via AC3 and relays an `ok: false` reason verbatim; generates a v4 UUID via `newId` and validates its shape (a malformed injected id ⇒ throws — pinned); writes via `putHumanDecision` with `reason` = the DTO's human-readable line, `railVersion`/`effectSchemaVersion` from the DTO (the caller's rails catalogue), `principal = canonicalTool`; the returned `id` is the repository's EFFECTIVE stored id (a refreshed duplicate returns the stored id, never the discarded fresh one — pinned) and `shortId` is derived from it. `deriveHumanDecisionShortIds(ids: string[]) → Map<id, shortId>` (exported, tested; the ONLY short-id function — no single-id wrapper, no compatibility shim, OWNER RULING 2026-09-06 "we don't need legacy code"): each id normalised once, the first 6 hex characters of the dash-free lowercase UUID, extended one character at a time only while another id in the list (this person's ACTIVE records) shares the prefix, resolved by prefix counting in one pass — so short ids are unique within a person's active list; `list({ appId, agentFolder, actingPersonId, limit? })` → active rows newest first; short ids are disambiguated against ALL of the person's active ids BEFORE `limit` is applied, so a truncated page never shows an ambiguous short id (pinned); `revoke({ appId, agentFolder, actingPersonId, recordId })` → the repository's result verbatim (the full record id; prefix resolution is T5b's); `countExactAllowsByTool(...)` → the repository's map. Tests (unit, in-memory fake repository): every refusal reason, once-never-remembered for each scalar mode, malformed injected id, a remembered allow and deny round-trip, refreshed duplicate returns the stored id, list is person-scoped, batch short-id derivation incl. a 6-char collision extending to 7 and a 500-id list resolved in one pass, revoke results. NO LEFTOVERS (owner ruling 2026-09-06): the diff carries no compatibility wrapper, shim, re-export kept "for callers", renamed-but-retained symbol or "legacy" naming; a reviewer finding one is a blocking finding.

non_blocking_findings.summary: [P2] Handle revocation before deriving the remembered row's short ID (apps/core/src/application/permissions/human-decision-memory-service.ts:119): After `putHumanDecision` commits, `remember` performs a separate active-only list and assumes the stored row is present.

[P2] Consolidate the duplicated human-decision UUID validator (apps/core/src/domain/ports/permission-decision-memory.ts:148): This port exports an `isHumanDecisionId` regex that duplicates the newly added validator in `shared/human-decision-id.ts`; different parts of the feature already consume different copies.
